classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied perpendicular to find a shared height and one base portion, transfer the height into the second triangle, and add the portions; distinguish subtraction for the external extension.

content.prompt: Find the length $XY$ in these diagrams. Answer to 1 d.p.

spec.description: Inverted triangle XYV with dashed perpendicular VF to the horizontal side XY. Ordinary blue source edges become black; the red construction remains semantically distinct.
spec.mathematics: XV = 3 cm; angle VXY = 50 degrees; angle XYV = 42 degrees; VF is perpendicular to XY.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; auxiliary vertex and foot names are omitted.

answer.worked:
Let $F$ be the foot of the perpendicular and $h$ its length.
$$\begin{align*}
h&=3\sin50^\circ\\
XF&=3\cos50^\circ\\
\tan42^\circ&=\frac{h}{FY}\\
FY&=\frac{3\sin50^\circ}{\tan42^\circ}\\
XY&=3\cos50^\circ+\frac{3\sin50^\circ}{\tan42^\circ}\\
XY&\approx4.5\text{ cm}
\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle VYR with Y marked by a solid point, X on the leftward horizontal extension, and an external dashed perpendicular XV.
spec.mathematics: X, Y and R are collinear in that order; XV = 10 mm; YR = 12 mm; angle YRV = 26 degrees; XV is perpendicular to XR.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; unlabelled source vertices remain unlabelled.

answer.worked:
Let $R$ be the rightmost vertex.
$$\begin{align*}
\tan26^\circ&=\frac{10}{XR}\\
XR&=\frac{10}{\tan26^\circ}\\
XY&=\frac{10}{\tan26^\circ}-12\\
XY&\approx8.5\text{ mm}
\end{align*}$$
